about: Geometer's price list of 21 Nov 2026: the proposed list of 20 Nov (plan decision 62, the higher chat caps), approved by the owner on 20 Nov ("commit, push and deploy") and in force from 21 Nov. No plan fee, allowance or outside rate moves. It raises the caps: each chat guest 40 model answers a day (ai.daily.customer-talk.per-guest, was 20), each shop 120 customer answers a day for each 1,000 messages of the plan (was 60), the monthly model budgets to INR 30, 90 and 300 for Basic, Business and Operations (were 20, 60, 200), fleet's ai.cap to INR 30 for each 1,000 messages (was 20), and a listings-only shop's customer answers to 60 a day (was 30). The shops' own budgets reach a shop with the next bundle deploy; fleet's ai.cap with the fleet deploy. The text of the 20 Nov proposal follows. Geometer's price list of 20 Nov 2026, PROPOSED (plan decision 62, owner 19 Nov: "yeah do higher chat caps"): it waits for the owner's yes with the fleet deploy and the bundle deploy, so nothing is capped from it until then. No plan fee, allowance or outside rate moves. It raises the caps of the 19 Nov list: each chat guest 40 model answers a day (was 20, a code constant, now ai.daily.customer-talk.per-guest), each shop 120 customer answers a day for each 1,000 messages of the plan (was 60), the monthly model budgets to INR 30, 90 and 300 for Basic, Business and Operations (were 20, 60, 200), fleet's ai.cap to INR 30 for each 1,000 messages (was 20), and a listings-only shop's customer answers to 60 a day (was 30). Cost to Geometer: at most INR 10, 30 and 100 a shop a month, only for a shop that uses all of it. The text of the 19 Nov list follows. Geometer's price list of 19 Nov 2026: the proposed list of 18 Nov (plan decision 60, "caps everywhere"), approved by the owner on 18 Nov ("approve the budget numbers as proposed") and in force from 19 Nov. No plan fee, allowance or outside rate moves. It adds the shop's own model budget by plan (Basic INR 20, Business INR 60, Operations INR 200 a month, a listings-only shop INR 6), the daily caps on each feature inside it, a monthly budget of INR 2,500 for the directory's buyer assistant (1,500 questions a day, 12 for each buyer), and raises fleet's outer wall ai.cap from INR 15 to INR 20 per 1,000 messages. The text of the 18 Nov proposal follows. A PROPOSED price list of 18 Nov 2026 (plan decision 60, "caps everywhere"): it waits for the owner's yes, so nothing is billed or capped from it until then. No plan fee, allowance or outside rate moves. It adds the shop's own MODEL BUDGET: one monthly budget in rupees for every model call a shop makes (the owner's talk, customers' open questions, listing drafts, the router's language step, voice), by plan, and a daily cap on each feature inside it (ids ai.budget.* and ai.daily.*; modules/budget/README.md says how they are used). It also proposes `ai.cap` (fleet's outer wall) at INR 20 per 1,000 messages instead of 15, so that wall sits at the same rupee as the shop's own budget (INR 20, 60 and 200 for 1,000, 3,000 and 10,000 messages) and fleet's check is the second line, not the first. Until the owner says yes the bundle writes no budget into any shop (it reads only lists in force) and fleet's cap stays INR 15. The text of the 14 Nov list follows. Geometer's price list of 14 Nov 2026. No price moves: it is the list of 11 Nov 2026 with only the note of the Operations plan reworded to plan decision 56 (docs/plans/implementation-plan.md): Operations is for a busy shop or service, for branches, or for three or more services together, and Business covers up to two services at one place. The text of the 11 Nov list follows. Geometer's price list of 11 Nov 2026, the one that puts the owner's decision of 10 Nov in force (decision 36, docs/plans/implementation-plan.md): the builder licence becomes INR 199 per live client business a month, flat (it was INR 149 in the list of 9 Nov; "we are providing many features to them anyways"). Nothing else changes: partners' plans (Basic INR 149, Business INR 299, Operations INR 999 flat), extra messages, WhatsApp and the recharge's payment fee at cost, the model-spend cap, the builders' fair-use line, the Innovator badge's 100 places, the guide.* suggestions and every outside rate are the 9 Nov list's, unchanged. A month is priced with the newest list dated on or before its last day, so this list prices all of November 2026; fleet had issued no invoice when it was made. The guide.* entries are what Geometer suggests a partner or builder charges, for the sell guides and the website's calculators; they are not Geometer's prices. This is the only place a price is written (prices/README.md): everything else reads this folder or a generated copy that a test compares with it. Amounts are whole numbers in micro-units of the rate's own currency (1,000,000 micro-rupees = INR 1), counts are whole numbers, and shares are basis points (10,000 = 100%). This file is never edited after it is committed: a changed price is a new file with a new date (node prices/new.ts <date>).

quality.official: Read on the provider's own current page.
quality.official-undated: Read on the provider's own page, but the page carries no date.
quality.second-hand: From a blog, a news item or a reseller's rate card, not the provider's own page. Confirm on an invoice.
quality.assumed: A round number chosen for the estimate, not read anywhere.
quality.conflicting: The provider's own pages disagree. The higher reading is used.

USD.note: The owner's rate of 7 Nov 2026: INR 94 to the US dollar (plan, decisions). The 5 Nov list used 88 (the economics document's assumption) and the 4 Nov list 90.

EUR.note: The research used INR 100 per EUR 1 as a round number and did not check the day's rate.

whatsapp.in.utility.note: INR 0.115 a utility message (reminders, owner notices) before 18% GST. Meta's own INR rate card is interactive and could not be read; three vendors show three figures, and the research reads INR 0.115 as Meta's base and the others as base plus a provider margin. Confirm on the chosen provider's invoice.

whatsapp.in.service.note: Replies inside the 24-hour window. From 1 Oct 2026 the first 1,000 a month per number are free and later ones cost the same as a utility message. The change is on Meta's developer page; the rupee figure is second-hand. whatsappbusiness.com still says they are free and looks stale.

whatsapp.in.marketing.note: About INR 0.86 a marketing message before 18% GST (about INR 1.02 with it), as the economics document's section 4.1 reads it from third-party pages. Broadcasts are never inside a plan, and today's templates send none, so this only prices a message that should not exist.

whatsapp.in.gst.note: 18% GST on Meta's charge per message, so a utility or charged service message costs about INR 0.136. The earlier lists left GST out of the WhatsApp rates; the plans pass the charge on with it.

whatsapp.provider.gupshup.note: US$0.001 a message, outgoing and incoming text, no monthly fee on the self-serve page. The page's table of Meta fees showed 0.0000 and may be a display problem. Partner terms are not public. Gupshup is the pilot pick only if it can sign its webhooks (research, question 1).

whatsapp.provider.360dialog.note: EUR 49 a number a month (regular plan), no markup on Meta's fees. The fallback if Gupshup cannot sign its webhooks.

razorpay.platform-fee.note: 2% of each successful payment. The page is dated May 2026. One line says Payment Links cost nothing extra and another says the no-code tools cost 0.2% plus gateway fees, so 2% is assumed until Razorpay confirms in writing. Paid by the shop to Razorpay, never by Geometer or the builder. Not returned when a payment is refunded.

razorpay.gst-on-fee.note: 18% GST on Razorpay's fee, as the pricing page (May 2026) states it. Confirm on a settlement statement.

model.claude-haiku-5-5.input.note: US$0.10 per million input tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens. Cache reads (US$0.01) are not used in the estimate.

model.claude-haiku-5-5.output.note: US$0.50 per million output tokens. It reasons by default, and reasoning is billed as output, so real usage can be higher.

model.gemini-3.1-flash-lite.input.note: US$0.25 per million input tokens, paid tier only (the free tier's text is used for training, which WhatsApp's terms forbid). The page has no date.

model.gemini-3.5-flash-lite.output.note: US$2.50 per million output tokens; thinking tokens count as output.

model.gpt-6-luna.input.note: US$0.10 per million input tokens. The page has no date.

plan.basic.fee.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov: Basic, no money moves, INR 149 a month for each shop that counts as live (was INR 99). Geometer's price to the partner, before GST.

plan.business.fee.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov: Business, deposits, refunds, fee collection or order advances with the owner's OK, INR 299 a month for each shop that counts as live (unchanged). Before GST.

plan.operations.fee.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov, worded as plan decision 56 (14 Nov): Operations is for a busy shop or service (usually above 3,000 messages), for branches, or for three or more services together; INR 999 a month flat (no longer "from", no bands). Business covers up to two services (templates) at one place. Each branch is its own shop. Before GST.

plan.basic.allowance.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov (unchanged): customer messages a month included in Basic. A message is one the agent handles; WhatsApp's own charges are separate and passed on at cost.

plan.business.allowance.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov (unchanged): customer messages a month included in Business.

plan.operations.allowance.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov (unchanged): customer messages a month included in Operations. Above it, extra messages at overage.extra, like every plan.

overage.extra.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov (unchanged): INR 49 for each 1,000 customer messages above a shop's allowance, paid from the partner's recharge balance in blocks of overage.block. Nothing is charged without the balance; an empty balance switches the shop to button menus, never to silence.

overage.block.note: Fleet's own choice: messages above the allowance are paid for 100 at a time (INR 4.90 at overage.extra), ahead of use, so each charge has a fixed name (shop, month, block number) and a repeated heartbeat cannot charge twice. An unused part of the last block is not given back at month end.

ai.cap.note: Decision 62 (owner, 19 Nov: "yeah do higher chat caps"), approved by the owner on 20 Nov ("commit, push and deploy") and in force from 21 Nov: INR 30 of model spend for each 1,000 messages a shop has, up from INR 20 (INR 15 before 19 Nov), so fleet's outer wall stays level with the shop's own budget (ai.budget.*: INR 30, 90 and 300 for 1,000, 3,000 and 10,000 messages) and is the second line, not the first. It is fleet's OUTER wall: once the month's model spend reaches it the language model is off for the rest of the month; rules and the decision model keep answering, and the Operator is told once. About INR 0.06 a talk turn, 0.04 a customer answer, 0.10 a four-language draft at the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash rate in modules/understanding/rates/2026-11-07.json.

whatsapp.pass-through.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov (unchanged since 5 Nov): WhatsApp is passed on at cost, never inside a plan price. 10,000 basis points is 100%: the partner's balance pays what Meta charges, with GST, plus the provider's per-message fee while the pilot uses Gupshup, at the exchange rate in this list. The recharge's payment fee is passed on too (recharge.payment-fee). No markup.

recharge.payment-fee.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov: the payment fee on the partner's balance top-up is passed on at cost and shown before paying. Razorpay's 2% (razorpay.platform-fee) plus 18% GST on it (razorpay.gst-on-fee) is 2.36%, on UPI too. It is taken off what is paid: a recharge of INR 1,000 adds INR 976.40 to the balance.

recharge.min.note: Fleet's own choice: the smallest recharge is INR 100 (what the partner pays, before the payment fee comes off). A recharge is a one-off Razorpay order and is never charged again on its own.

recharge.max.note: Fleet's own choice: the largest recharge is INR 50,000, so a typing mistake cannot become a large order.

recharge.expiry-months.note: Decided by the owner, 5 Nov: a recharge expires 12 months after it was granted.

recharge.warn.note: Decided by the owner, 5 Nov: the partner is warned once 80% of the unexpired recharge is used, and a shop is warned once 80% of its included messages are used.

licence.builder.fee.note: Decided by the owner, 10 Nov (decision 36): a builder pays INR 199 a month, flat, for each client business that counts as live (15 or more live days, the partners' rule), for all of that business's agents, templates or the builder's own (was INR 149 from 9 Nov; "we are providing many features to them anyways"). No allowance, no balance, no volume discount, no agency plan. Before GST. Partners' prices are unchanged.

licence.builder.fair-use.agents.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov: the licence covers up to 5 live agents for one client business. Above that, or for a company running agents for itself, it is a Guard contract.

licence.builder.fair-use.actions.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov: the licence covers up to 25,000 guarded actions a month for one client business (a typical salon makes about 1,750, a busy one about 6,000). Above that it is a Guard contract.

innovator.places.note: Decided by the owner, 9 Nov (kept from 5 Nov): the Innovator badge and the template vote go to the first 100 builders and partners with a shop live; the registry refuses a 101st. A badge, not a discount: there is no first-100 price.

guide.basic.shop-min.note: Geometer's suggested shop price for Basic, lower end: INR 499 a month (the partner decides).

guide.basic.shop-max.note: Geometer's suggested shop price for Basic, upper end: INR 699 a month.

guide.business.shop-min.note: Geometer's suggested shop price for Business, lower end: INR 999 a month.

guide.business.shop-max.note: Geometer's suggested shop price for Business, upper end: INR 1,499 a month.

guide.operations.shop-min.note: Geometer's suggested shop price for Operations: INR 3,499 a month and up.

guide.basic.setup-min.note: Suggested one-time setup fee for Basic, lower end: INR 999. The partner keeps all of it.

guide.basic.setup-max.note: Suggested one-time setup fee for Basic, upper end: INR 1,999.

guide.business.setup-min.note: Suggested one-time setup fee for Business, lower end: INR 1,999. The partner keeps all of it.

guide.business.setup-max.note: Suggested one-time setup fee for Business, upper end: INR 2,999.

guide.operations.setup-min.note: Suggested one-time setup fee for Operations: INR 4,999 and up, quoted by the partner (an estimate).

guide.builder.client-fee.note: The builder calculator's default monthly fee a builder charges a client: INR 2,500. The builder sets it.

guide.builder.own-costs.note: An estimate of a builder's own running costs per client: a server share of about INR 100, a model key of about INR 100 and Meta's messages of about INR 60-100. A WhatsApp platform with a monthly fee per number adds about INR 1,350-2,800.

guide.basic.whatsapp.note: An estimate of WhatsApp at cost for a small (Basic) shop on the pilot route (Meta plus Gupshup's fee), with the recharge's payment fee: about INR 90 a month.

guide.business.whatsapp.note: An estimate of WhatsApp at cost for a typical (Business) shop on the pilot route, with the recharge's payment fee: about INR 295 a month.

guide.operations.whatsapp.note: An estimate of WhatsApp at cost for a busy (Operations) shop on the pilot route, with the recharge's payment fee: about INR 1,316 a month.

ai.budget.basic.note: Decision 62 (owner, 19 Nov: "yeah do higher chat caps"), approved by the owner on 20 Nov ("commit, push and deploy") and in force from 21 Nov: the most model spend a Basic shop may make in a month, for every feature together (INR 30, 20% of the INR 149 fee; the same as ai.cap for its 1,000 messages), up from INR 20. Used up: the language model is off until the 1st; buttons, rules, fixed answers and the plain listing form go on. The owner is told at 80% of it and once more when it is used up.

ai.budget.business.note: Decision 62 (owner, 19 Nov: "yeah do higher chat caps"), approved by the owner on 20 Nov ("commit, push and deploy") and in force from 21 Nov: the most model spend a Business shop may make in a month, for every feature together (INR 90, 30% of the INR 299 fee; the same as ai.cap for its 3,000 messages), up from INR 60. Used up: the language model is off until the 1st; buttons, rules, fixed answers and the plain listing form go on. The owner is told at 80% of it and once more when it is used up. Fleet's own alert at 50% of the plan price (decision 23) stays.

ai.budget.operations.note: Decision 62 (owner, 19 Nov: "yeah do higher chat caps"), approved by the owner on 20 Nov ("commit, push and deploy") and in force from 21 Nov: the most model spend a Operations shop may make in a month, for every feature together (INR 300, 30% of the INR 999 fee; the same as ai.cap for its 10,000 messages), up from INR 200. Used up: the language model is off until the 1st; buttons, rules, fixed answers and the plain listing form go on. The owner is told at 80% of it and once more when it is used up.

ai.budget.listings-only.note: Approved by the owner on 18 Nov ("approve the budget numbers as proposed"), in force from 19 Nov: the small budget of a free listings-only shop (plan decision 60 Phase C), which Geometer pays: INR 6, about 60 four-language drafts, or 100 answers to people asking about a listing. Its feature list is only the owner's talk, drafts and 'Ask about this'.

ai.budget.discovery.note: Approved by the owner on 18 Nov ("approve the budget numbers as proposed"), in force from 19 Nov: the monthly budget of the directory's buyer assistant (a model only at the buyer's end, decision 60), for every buyer together: INR 2,500 (about 50,000 questions at INR 0.05), paid by Geometer. Plain search never stops. A guess, to be set again with the first real month's spend.

ai.daily.owner-talk.note: Approved by the owner on 18 Nov ("approve the budget numbers as proposed"), in force from 19 Nov: the most owner-talk turns (words the rules did not read, answered by the model) a shop may use in a day. Past it the owner gets the buttons and fixed answers, and is told once that day.

ai.daily.listing-draft.note: Approved by the owner on 18 Nov ("approve the budget numbers as proposed"), in force from 19 Nov: the most listing drafts the model may write for a shop in a day (a refused or failed draft counts: it cost tokens). Past it the owner is sent to the plain Add to my page form.

ai.daily.customer-talk.per: 1,000 messages of the plan's allowance, a day
ai.daily.customer-talk.note: Decision 62 (owner, 19 Nov: "yeah do higher chat caps"), approved by the owner on 20 Nov ("commit, push and deploy") and in force from 21 Nov: the most open questions the model may answer for all customers of a shop together in a day, for each 1,000 messages of its plan's allowance (120 Basic, 360 Business, 1,200 Operations), up from 60. One guest's own limit is ai.daily.customer-talk.per-guest. Past it customers get the rule-based reading and the shop's template answers; only the owner is told, once that day.

ai.daily.customer-talk.per-guest.note: Decision 62 (owner, 19 Nov: "yeah do higher chat caps"), approved by the owner on 20 Nov ("commit, push and deploy") and in force from 21 Nov: the most typed sends that may ask the model for one chat guest (a customer on the shop's page) in a day, up from 20. It was a code constant (CHAT_LIMITS.modelTurnsPerDay in modules/channels/chat.ts) and now lives only here: the bundle writes it into the shop's runtime.json as budget.guestTurnsPerDay. After it the rules and the buttons answer, as in button mode.

ai.daily.router.per: 1,000 messages of the plan's allowance, a day
ai.daily.router.note: Approved by the owner on 18 Nov ("approve the budget numbers as proposed"), in force from 19 Nov: the most times the router may ask its language step in a day, for each 1,000 messages of the plan's allowance (100 Basic, 300 Business, 1,000 Operations). Past it the rules and the decision model read the message, and what neither can read gets the menu.

ai.daily.listings-only.owner-talk.note: Approved by the owner on 18 Nov ("approve the budget numbers as proposed"), in force from 19 Nov: owner-talk turns a day for a free listings-only shop.

ai.daily.listings-only.customer-talk.note: Decision 62 (owner, 19 Nov: "yeah do higher chat caps"), approved by the owner on 20 Nov ("commit, push and deploy") and in force from 21 Nov: answers a day to people asking about a listing, for all of a listings-only shop's visitors together, up from 30.

ai.daily.discovery.note: Approved by the owner on 18 Nov ("approve the budget numbers as proposed"), in force from 19 Nov: the most buyer-assistant calls the directory may make in a day, for every buyer together (INR 2,500 a month is about INR 80 a day).

ai.daily.discovery.per-buyer.note: Approved by the owner on 18 Nov ("approve the budget numbers as proposed"), in force from 19 Nov: the most buyer-assistant questions one buyer (a session or an address, never a name) may ask in a day.

notPriced.sarvam-105b-conversations: Sarvam's price page shows display names only, so which listed price belongs to this model is not confirmed. https://www.sarvam.ai/api-pricing
notPriced.meta-rate-card: Meta's own INR rate card (interactive) could not be read.
